ingredient/dry-vermouth.behaviour: A dry white wine strengthened with spirit and scented with herbs, bark and peel. It is sharper and more aromatic than plain white wine. A splash dissolves the browned bits in a pan, and it is boiled down so that its raw taste of spirit goes and only the acid and the herbal scent are left. A cook who has no white wine often reaches for it in a cream sauce or a fish dish.
